findings: 2026-11-05: drafted for Mathematics 11 Unit 1 (owner request): English and a teacher-style Roman Urdu lesson; the book's content in order with our clearly labelled teaching notes; worked examples step by step with reasons; results verified with sympy.

Book correction: The book prints this heading as 1.4.1, a number it already used for “Properties of Cube Roots of Unity” (book page 12). We keep the printed number so you can find it in your textbook; only the numbering is wrong.

Book correction: In Example 12, Step I, the book prints “Put r\cos\theta = 1 and r\cos\theta = \sqrt{3}”. The second equation should be r\sin\theta = \sqrt{3}, because the imaginary part of r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta) is r\sin\theta. The rest of the book's solution (r = 2, \theta = 60^{\circ}) is correct.
